bibliographic.title: Leveraging ChatGPT and Other Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Based Applications in the Hospitality and Tourism Industry: Practices, Challenges, and Research Agenda
bibliographic.authors: Yogesh K Dwivedi; Neeraj Pandey; Wendy Currie; Adrian Micu
bibliographic.venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management
bibliographic.citation_apa: Dwivedi, Y. K., Pandey, N., Currie, W., & Micu, A. (2024). Leveraging ChatGPT and other generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based applications in the hospitality and tourism industry: Practices, challenges, and research agenda. International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management, 36(1), 1-12. https://doi.org/10.1108/IJCHM-05-2023-0686

methodology.method_family: literature and practice analysis with research agenda development
methodology.technology_context: generative artificial intelligence (ChatGPT, Bard), self-serving technologies (SSTs), customer interface and backend applications

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The available text describes a conceptual hospitality/tourism research agenda on GenAI adoption and implementation challenges; it does not address conversational governance mechanisms, oversight, auditability, or regulated high-stakes deployment contexts central to the review scope.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper explicitly discusses ChatGPT and generative AI and mentions challenges from the perspectives of companies, customers, and regulators, the provided evidence is limited to front matter and abstract. The focus is sectoral adoption in hospitality and tourism rather than conversational AI governance in regulated environments. No explicit treatment of guardrails, observability, human oversight, accountability frameworks, or compliance-oriented conversational system design appears in the supplied text.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only pages 1-3 (HAL front matter, author list, and abstract) were supplied; governance-related terms may appear later in the full article and should be verified before final exclusion.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is constrained to abstract-level evidence. The paper presents itself as a literature-and-practice analysis proposing a research agenda, not as an empirical governance evaluation. Limitations, ethics, and detailed methods are not visible in the supplied excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: For the target review on conversational governance of LLMs in regulated settings, relevance is low despite clear GenAI focus. Confidence is limited because only the abstract/front matter was available; the study also appears conceptual rather than empirically grounded in governance practices.

coding.theme: GenAI adoption in hospitality and tourism

synthesis.main_claim: Integrating generative AI technologies such as ChatGPT will have a transformational impact on hospitality and tourism, while implementation poses challenges for companies, customers, and regulators.
synthesis.contribution: The paper analyzes existing literature and practices and outlines a novel research agenda for scholars and practitioners planning to use generative AI tools such as ChatGPT in hospitality and tourism businesses.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text does not report empirical methods, sample, governance mechanisms, or study limitations; appraisal is based only on abstract-level claims.
synthesis.use_in_review: Not recommended as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance in regulated LLM systems; at most potentially useful as contextual background on sectoral GenAI adoption and generic stakeholder challenges if later full-text review confirms absence of governance content.
